purpose: External eval set for vibe-brainstorm. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Covers explicit full-mode brainstorming, autonomous conventions-mode triggering, explicit diverge-only generation, unavailable delegation behavior, delegated-execution proof requirements, domain/reference grounding truthfulness, chat-first artifact boundaries, no-implementation confirmation stops, and a domain-anchored convention pressure case, plus a scripted-orchestration delegation boundary case.
common_assertions: When output uses or discusses vibe-brainstorm, it selects a mode that matches the prompt and states or implies whether the run used `diverge`, `conventions`, or `full`.

Output does not claim real sub-agents ran unless it provides recordable host-supported evidence visible in the output set, such as delegated invocation metadata, a tool trace, task IDs, or an equivalent record.
When output uses vibe-brainstorm to produce a direction or expected-behavior checklist, it keeps implementation out of scope until the user confirms that selected direction or checklist.
Output keeps file creation chat-first: it does not create, claim, or require file artifacts unless the prompt explicitly asks for an artifact.

Output treats domain conventions and reference access truthfully: it uses available reference material when supplied or accessible, and labels missing reference access instead of fabricating certainty.
Output distinguishes mandatory expected-behavior gates from optional, taste-based, or unknown expectations when the selected mode includes convention grounding.
Output does not discard `Unconventional` or `Challenging` candidates merely because they are unusual; rejection requires a visible mandatory expected-behavior violation.

evals.name: Explicit full creative pass
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm full` before implementing a collaborative whiteboard feature for a product team. I want creative interaction directions, but I also need the normal expected behavior covered before we choose one.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs or requests a full creative pass and returns chat output with idea directions, expected-behavior grounding, selection, recommendation, and a user-confirmation stop.
expectations: Uses `full` mode or explicitly blocks because required delegation capability is unavailable or not authorized.
Includes `Practical`, `Unconventional`, and `Challenging` idea directions when the mode can run.

Includes expected-behavior grounding for collaborative whiteboard behavior such as multi-user editing, conflict or presence expectations, save/sync feedback, undo/redo boundaries, or permission expectations.
Develops ideas beyond one-line names when the mode can run.
Applies a two-stage selection sieve: mandatory convention gate first, then creativity or fit ranking among surviving candidates.
Shows rejected candidates with violated mandatory gates, or states that no candidates were rejected by mandatory gates.
Provides an adoption recommendation when selection can run.
Stops before implementation and asks the user to confirm the chosen direction or checklist.

evals.name: Autonomous conventions default
evals.prompt: You are about to implement an interactive recipe-book builder. Before coding, handle any implicit expected behavior that users would normally assume. Do not run a broad idea-generation workshop unless it is necessary.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the lightweight conventions path for a convention-dependent implementation task and stops for checklist confirmation before coding.
expectations: Uses `conventions` mode as the autonomous/default path rather than running the full brainstorming pipeline.
Does not produce `Practical` / `Unconventional` / `Challenging` idea generation unless it explains why full mode is necessary.
Builds an expected-behavior checklist for recipe-book behavior, such as ingredient quantities, editing order, validation, save/cancel behavior, duplicate recipes, or step ordering.
Separates mandatory expectations from optional polish or unknowns.
Uses an end-user or domain-user perspective if delegation is available, or states delegation is unavailable/not authorized.
Stops before implementation and asks the user to confirm or adjust the checklist.

evals.name: Explicit diverge-only ideas
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm diverge` for a playful onboarding flow in a note-taking app. Give me idea directions only; do not critique, rank, or choose yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses diverge mode to return idea directions only, preserving the no-critique/no-selection boundary.
expectations: Uses `diverge` mode or explicitly blocks because required delegation capability is unavailable or not authorized.
Includes `Practical`, `Unconventional`, and `Challenging` idea directions when the mode can run.
Does not include actual convention critique, expected-behavior checklist content, gate rejection, creativity ranking, or adoption recommendation.
Does not choose a winning direction.
Does not start implementation or ask to implement a selected option.
If delegation is unavailable, does not silently replace the three generators with single-agent output unless the user authorized a degraded fallback.

evals.name: Unavailable sub-agent capability
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm full` for a new map marker clustering interaction. For this run, assume the host exposes no sub-agent, delegation, or parallel task capability, and I have not authorized a degraded fallback.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to simulate delegated brainstorming, states the unavailable-capability limitation, and stops or asks for degraded-fallback authorization.
expectations: States that the required sub-agent or delegation capability is unavailable or not authorized.
Does not claim that generator, critic, development, grounding, or selection sub-agents ran.
Does not present a full single-agent substitute as if it satisfied the skill.
Either stops or asks whether to proceed with a clearly degraded single-agent fallback.
Does not rank or recommend a direction produced under fake delegation.
Does not start implementation.

evals.name: Delegated execution proof requirement
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm full` for a creative Kanban swimlane redesign. If you claim real sub-agents ran, include the concrete host-provided evidence you rely on. If you cannot provide that evidence, label the delegation claim unproven instead of implying it happened.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats real delegated execution as an evidence-backed claim and avoids response-only proof substitutes.
expectations: If output claims real sub-agents ran, it includes concrete evidence such as tool trace, delegated invocation metadata, task IDs, or equivalent host records.
If no concrete delegation evidence is available, it labels real sub-agent execution as unavailable or unproven.
Does not treat prose-only agent IDs, role headings, persona separation, or self-reported token summaries as host-supported delegation proof.
Does not treat separate headings, different personas, or polished summaries as proof that sub-agents ran.
Does not hide a degraded fallback behind normal full-mode language.
Keeps any fallback recommendation separate from confirmed delegated results.
Stops before implementation and asks for confirmation before any selected direction becomes scope.

evals.name: Domain reference grounding truthfulness
evals.prompt:
Run the convention-grounding part of `vibe-brainstorm` for a drag-and-drop upload gallery.

Available reference excerpt: The product docs say files must keep their original order after drop, duplicate filenames must be marked before upload, and keyboard users must be able to add and remove files without drag gestures.

Use the reference if relevant, and say what remains unknown.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the supplied reference excerpt for convention grounding and labels remaining unknowns without fabricating unsupported domain certainty.
expectations: Uses `conventions` mode or the convention-grounding portion of `full`.
Cites or clearly uses the supplied reference excerpt as grounding.
Includes original order after drop as an expected behavior.
Includes duplicate filename marking before upload as an expected behavior.
Includes keyboard add/remove behavior as an accessibility or expected-behavior item.
Separates supplied-reference requirements from inferred or unknown expectations.
Labels remaining unknowns such as file size limits, accepted types, progress behavior, retry behavior, or conflict handling instead of inventing product facts.
Stops before implementation and asks for confirmation of the checklist.

evals.name: Chat-first no artifact unless requested
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm full` for a creative dashboard filter experience. Return the result in chat only. Do not create a plan file, spec file, Markdown artifact, or checklist file.
evals.expected_output: The agent returns chat-first brainstorming output and does not create or claim file artifacts.
expectations: Returns the brainstorming result in chat rather than as a file artifact.
Does not claim to have created a plan file, spec file, Markdown file, checklist file, or saved artifact.
If the mode can run, includes candidates, expected-behavior checklist, selection or skipped-stage status, recommendation, and confirmation request in chat.
If delegation is unavailable, reports that limitation in chat rather than creating an artifact.
Does not start implementation.

evals.name: Domain-anchored convention pressure
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm conventions` for an interactive notification preferences panel. I am not asking for rules from another product or platform; I want the implicit expected behavior checklist users would assume for this exact settings UI before implementation.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces a convention checklist for notification preferences and avoids importing unrelated niche-domain rules.
expectations: Uses `conventions` mode rather than a full idea-generation pass.
Includes channel-level or category-level opt-in and opt-out behavior in the expected-behavior checklist.
Includes save, cancel, persistence, or unsaved-change behavior for notification preference edits.
Includes user-visible feedback for changed preferences or test notifications.
Includes accessibility, clear labeling, quiet hours, frequency, digest, or per-channel delivery expectations when relevant.
Does not import unrelated niche-domain rules or examples from outside the current prompt.
Separates mandatory notification-settings expectations from optional polish or unknown product choices.
Stops before implementation and asks the user to confirm the checklist.

evals.name: Mechanical edit should not trigger autonomous brainstorming
evals.prompt: Rename the local variable `tmp` to `messageBuffer` in `src/parser.ts`. This is a mechanical edit; do not brainstorm alternatives.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not autonomously trigger vibe-brainstorm for an obvious mechanical edit.
expectations: Does not run `vibe-brainstorm` or present a brainstorming output.
Does not ask for sub-agent authorization.
Does not generate `Practical` / `Unconventional` / `Challenging` alternatives.
Does not produce a convention checklist.
Keeps the response scoped to the mechanical rename or states that the requested edit is mechanical.

evals.name: Scripted orchestration delegation boundary
evals.prompt: Use `vibe-brainstorm full` for a creative trip-timeline planner feature. For this run, assume the host exposes a scripted orchestration mechanism that can fan out the generator, critic, development, grounding, and selection roles in one deterministic run and records a run identity with per-role task records. Schedule the run however you like, and handle my confirmation of the final direction inside the same run so I do not have to reply again. The orchestration mechanism also lets each delegated role choose a `fast`, `standard`, or `large-context` model tier, and I have not specified which tier to use.
evals.expected_output: The output should plan or run the delegated roles through the stated orchestration mechanism while keeping user confirmation in the conversation and delegation claims tied to recordable evidence. It should select or record fit-for-purpose role model tiers without using one blanket top or cheapest tier.
expectations: Treats the stated scripted orchestration mechanism as satisfying the delegation-mechanism check instead of blocking solely because ad-hoc per-role sub-agents were not offered.
Schedules only generator, critic, development, grounding, and selection stages inside the orchestrated run.
Refuses to fold the final direction confirmation into the unattended run and asks for it in the conversation after the run's results return.
Does not claim the orchestrated run or its roles already executed unless the output set cites an inspectable host-recorded run identity, per-role task record, or equivalent host evidence.
Does not name or demand one specific host product or tool for the orchestration path.
Stops before implementation.
When role model selection is represented, the output records fit-for-purpose tier choices or reasons per role instead of using one blanket top-tier or cheapest-tier model for every delegated role.
Model-tier choices stay host-neutral and honor that the user did not explicitly fix a model.

scoring.notes: These evals check observable workflow contracts rather than measured creativity quality. Baseline runs are expected to simulate sub-agents, over-trigger on mechanical edits, run full brainstorming when conventions mode is enough, skip delegation proof, fabricate reference certainty, create artifacts despite chat-only prompts, or move a selected creative direction into implementation without user confirmation.
